name: Generated Artifact Ownership
description: Define and enforce ownership of generated artifacts. Every generated artifact knows what generated it (tool/command identity), when (timestamp + source commit), and from which source (input file hash). Implement source-change detection that invalidates dependent artifacts and triggers rebuild scheduling.
purpose: Without ownership tracking, stale artifacts silently poison downstream consumers — type definitions from out-of-date sources, schemas that no longer match implementation, test fixtures that test the wrong thing. Ownership enables accurate rebuild decisions and trust in artifact freshness.
acceptanceCriteria: Every artifact entry records generator identity (tool name + version)
Every artifact entry records generation timestamp
Every artifact entry records source hash(es) that produced it
Every artifact entry records the source commit hash at generation time
Source-change detection watches tracked source files for hash changes
When a source file changes, all artifacts derived from it are marked stale
Stale artifacts trigger a rebuild notification or scheduled rebuild
Artifact ownership chain is queryable: source → generated artifacts → downstream consumers
Rebuild is idempotent: re-running generator with same inputs produces same outputs (verified by hash)
